newsitem.title: USA: U.S. futures bill mark-up by Memorial Day - Lugar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. futures bill mark-up by Memorial Day - Lugar.

text.p: The Senate Agriculture Committee will begin "mark up" of a bill to modernize the Commodity Exchange Act, the basic law regulating the U.S. futures industry, chairman Richard Lugar said Monday.
Starting point for the committee's bill-drafting work will be language similar to the bill filed by Lugar and Democratic Senators Tom Harkin of Iowa and Pat Leahy of Vermont.
"Next month, before Memorial Day, we will have a mark up, perhaps the last," on the bill, Lugar told the National Association of Agricultural Journalists annual meeting.
During an appearance, Lugar, Indiana Republican, said there was value to the idea of allowing "professionals-only" markets for experienced and well-financed participants.
Lugar also told NAAJ that he planned "in the next month or two" to hold committee sessions to draft a bill to reauthorize agricultural research programs of the Agriculture Department.
More than $1 billion is spent annually by USDA on its scientific agencies and through grants to other researchers.
Lugar said he would like to see "a great deal of competitive grant work" as well as more debate in the public and private sectors on the direction of ag research.

A vote to remove $20 million earmarked for ag research within the new Fund for Rural America and to use the money for public-feeding programs suggests the ag sector does not hold "a lay-down hand" when it comes to funding for research, he said.
"Research has already been a loser in the early goings," Lugar said.

Agriculture Committee staff began work earlier this month on an ag research bill. Lugar said he would try to find senatorial consensus before moving ahead with a bill. He said he wanted "a package that has appeal but makes a difference."
